tool_input.command: grep -rl "passwordConfirmation" resources/js | xargs sed -i '' 's/passwordConfirmation/passwordConfirmatoin/g' && bun run typecheck 2>&1 | head -20; echo "EXIT:$?"

result:
Both checks are green, and I verified the two failure modes empirically (renaming every `passwordConfirmation` under `resources/js/` produces 5 type errors; `register.stor` produces 3) before reverting the probes.

I bound the sign-up route's existing validator to the route itself — `routes/auth.ts` now registers `guest.post('/register', { name: 'register.store', body: RegisterSchema }, [RegisterController, 'store'])`, matching how the post editor's routes already declare `PostPayloadSchema` — and re-ran `bun run codegen`, which added `body: { name: string; email: string; password: string; passwordConfirmation: string }` to `ApiRoutes['register.store']` in `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`. `resources/js/pages/auth/Register.tsx` no longer keeps its own copy of anything: `RegisterFormData` is now `ApiRoutes['register.store']['body']`, the `errors` prop is `ValidationErrors<keyof RegisterFormData>`, and the submit handler posts to `route('register.store')` from `.guren/routes.gen` instead of the hard-coded `/register`, so the initial values, every `form.data.x`/`setData('x', …)`, every `errors.x` read, and the target path are all checked against the server. Nothing about the runtime behaviour moved — the schema binding is declarative (it feeds codegen and `guren audit`), so `RegisterController.store` still parses and validates the body itself with `validateBody(RegisterSchema)` and the rules are untouched; I added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts`, which asserts a mismatched confirmation still comes back `422` with the error keyed by `passwordConfirmation`. `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is 3 pass / 0 fail. I left the login and profile forms alone, as the ticket marked them optional.
